admin_throwaway.title: Sign in as a throwaway test account
admin_throwaway.description:
Sign this box in as a throwaway test account, <name>@bot.yak.sh. Without a name, a fresh probe-<random> address. The sign-in code is read from the letter in this graph. The current account stays as it was: name the new one per command with --as.

  yak admin throwaway cookbook

admin_accept.title: Accept an invitation addressed to this account
admin_accept.description:
Accept the signed invitation link in a local mail entity using this account’s session. The link and session are never printed.

  yak admin accept E-41217 --as admin@bot.yak.sh

Requires the website session retained by a code sign-in; browser OAuth sign-ins have none.

admin_link.title: Make a standing sign-in link
admin_link.description:
One URL that signs its holder in as this account until it expires, or --revoke to take one back by its id.

  yak admin throwaway reviewer && yak admin link --days=90 --as=reviewer
  yak admin link --revoke=3f2a --as=reviewer

Requires the website session retained by a code sign-in; browser OAuth sign-ins have none.

admin_fee.description:

  yak admin fee 250 --as admin@bot.yak.sh

admin_move.title: Rehearse or run the store mover in every yaks.app store
admin_move.description:
The store mover brings a store's rows into a new shape from its alarm, a batch at a time (workers/yak/mover.ts). This asks every store in turn, the app stores first and the directory last, and prints a line per store and rule as it goes. --rehearse moves each rule's rows inside a transaction the store rolls back, up to twenty batches, and says what it found and moved, any failure, and how long the store took to answer; without it each store is woken to move what it owes, a few a minute, and says where each rule stands. A space or space/app narrows it. The platform’s act, so the selected account must have the platform role.

  yak admin move --rehearse --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin move --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin move ada --rehearse --as admin@bot.yak.sh

pace.description: stores a minute, 0 for each as soon as the last answers (5 for a wake, 0 for a rehearsal)

admin_tunnel.title: A space's tunnel to a machine
admin_tunnel.description:
The tunnel a space has to a machine, whose server the space's apps reach through the tunnel's gateway (a vpc_services door in their config), at the paths its @yaks/tunnel config opens. With no act, what the tunnel is. connect makes a tunnel, its service to the port given, and the gateway; rotate puts the gateway again, and gives the tunnel a new token where the platform made it; adopt records a tunnel and service made elsewhere with a gateway in front, and is the platform's act. A token answered is kept in this graph's vault as TUNNEL_TOKEN without printing it, where @yaks/tunnel's service reads it. disconnect removes the tunnel.

  yak admin tunnel yak --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin tunnel yak adopt --tunnel <id> --service <id> --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin tunnel ada connect --port 5173

act.description: what to change; nothing reads the tunnel

port.description: connect: the port the machine's server listens on

admin_query.description:

  yak admin query jeff .kind=note

admin_apply.title: Apply bundles to an app’s store
admin_apply.description:
Create, patch or delete rows in an app’s store as this account, through the connector’s graph_apply: the store’s rules and journal hold, and the write is recorded as the account. The space’s owner and the platform’s admin write any app’s rows; --check rehearses the batch and keeps nothing.

  yak admin apply yourname/vale '[{"entity": {"eid": "<eid>"}, "sfx": {"notes": "chime"}}]' --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin apply jeff/recipes @fix.json --check --as admin@bot.yak.sh

admin_upload.title: Upload a local file to an app's blob store
admin_upload.description:
Send one local file through an app's /api/blob door. It writes the content and attachment rows and returns the content-addressed URL.  its app role must allow writes. The file name defaults to the local basename and mime defaults to application/octet-stream.

  yak admin upload yourname/vale /tmp/theme.mp3 --mime audio/mpeg --name mossvale-theme.mp3 --as admin@bot.yak.sh

admin_push.title: Push a directory to a yaks.app app
admin_push.description:
Make an app hold exactly the files in a directory, through the connector's own tools: app_new when the app does not exist yet, app_files for new or changed files (base64 for any that is not UTF-8), a delete for each file the directory no longer has, then app_deploy when files need releasing. An unchanged, released app is left alone. Git is the app's only source. The app's slug is the directory's name unless --app names another; --space picks one when the account has several.

  yak admin push apps/mail --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin push apps/mail --app inbox --space jeff --title Inbox --as admin@bot.yak.sh

The base version is remembered separately for each source directory, account and target. A stale base answers with the live files the deploy would remove or replace; repeat with --confirm to deploy them. A base past live (rolled back elsewhere) writes nothing until --confirm, which then deploys over what is live.

confirm.description: deploy after reviewing the files a stale base would remove or replace

dir.description: the directory holding the app's files

app.description: the app's slug, when it is not the directory's name

space.description: the space, when the account has several

title.description: the title a new app is created with; the slug unless named

admin_deploys.description: Recent yaks.app uploads and deployments with their commits and live times; ~ marks a commit inferred by time. Migration boundaries survive code rollbacks, and unknown history refuses a rollback. Infrastructure requires the platform admin or the configured person’s own account.

admin_errors.title: List yaks.app failures by tracker bug
admin_errors.description: Every unresolved tracker bug (not resolved or archived), however old, newest first. No time window by default; since optionally narrows by last seen. Thrown or caught: lifetime count, first and last seen, global bug id, place and message. Then the time to fix of the bugs resolved in the window (a week without since): median and worst, first seen or regressed to resolved; and how long the oldest open bug has been open. Then people's letters to the platform's addresses in the same window: how many, how many have a reply in their thread with median and worst time to answer, and each one still unanswered (archive a letter that needs no answer). Reads the tracker through its signed door using the remote URL and vault reference in tracker.json beside this graph; `admin tail` watches live traffic. Infrastructure requires the platform admin or the configured person’s own account.

since.description: optional duration narrowing bugs by last seen (for example 7d); no time window by default

admin_gallery.title: Decide, code-review or list a gallery app
admin_gallery.description:
As the platform admin, act on a gallery request. code-review records your review of the code of an app somebody else asked into the gallery, which comes to you as a task, and sends the platform’s owner its review request with your verdict and findings. approve and decline answer a request, and list puts a published app in the gallery at once, skipping review: do those only when the platform’s owner asks, and name him with --by. The session is recorded from this call.

  yak admin gallery acme/todo code-review --verdict approve --findings @findings.md --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin gallery jeff/housebook approve --by jeff@yak.sh --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin gallery yourname/garden list --by jeff@yak.sh --as admin@bot.yak.sh

decision.description: approve or decline answers a request (gallery_review); list puts the app in the gallery now, with no request and no review (app_set gallery: true, review: false); code-review records your code review and sends the request on (gallery_code_review)

verdict.description: with code-review: whether the code should be listed

findings.description: with code-review: what the review found, as text or @file

by.description: who the decision is recorded as: the platform owner’s address when he asked for it; default the calling agent’s project

reason.description: why a request was approved or declined
